i.norm: Verifies that tag lookup is case-insensitive under htmlDefault settings, even when the JVM default Locale changes (Turkish locale, for example, uppercases 'i' differently). When looking up through a shared TagSet, identical tags should be the exact same instance.
Tag.valueOf creates a fresh TagSet each call, so the two tags are equal but not identical
A shared TagSet caches tags, so the same normalized name returns the identical instance

Verifies the interaction between ParseSettings and Tag identity: - Tag.valueOf creates a new TagSet on every call, so identical lookups yield distinct instances. - ParseSettings.preserveCase retains the original casing in the tag name. - A shared TagSet with htmlDefault normalises case, returning the same cached instance. - A shared TagSet without explicit ParseSettings does NOT normalise case, yielding distinct instances.
Each Tag.valueOf call builds a fresh TagSet, so no instance sharing occurs here
preserveCase keeps the supplied casing; htmlDefault normalises to lower-case
A single shared TagSet normalises lookups with htmlDefault: same instance returned
Without ParseSettings the TagSet does not normalise case, so different names → different instances
